Reference · settings

Configuration

Every setting the service reads, with the exact key, the environment variable that overrides it, the default in the code, and the rule that refuses a bad value at start-up rather than halfway through a run.

Sections 13 in the settings tree Override order defaults, file, environment, CLI Formats TOML, YAML, JSON by suffix Prefix SQT_SERIES_, nested with __ Durations two different syntaxes — read the note

How a setting gets its value

Four sources can set a value. They are applied in a fixed order, so you always know which one wins. A setting the environment touches ignores the file entirely — that is deliberate, and it is why a container variable reliably beats a baked-in config.

  1. The default in the codeEvery setting has one, and it is what you get with no configuration at all. Every default on this page was read out of src/sqtseries/config.py.
  2. The config fileNamed by --config, or by SQT_SERIES_CONFIG_FILE. TOML, YAML or JSON, chosen by suffix.
  3. Environment variablesAnything prefixed SQT_SERIES_. A variable beats the file for the same leaf, always.
  4. --dbApplied after everything else, so it wins over the file and the environment for the database path.
The file does not simply override the environment

Settings loaders usually let an init argument beat an environment variable. Here that would be wrong: a file could shadow a variable that an operator set on purpose. So the loader reads the file, works out which leaves the environment actually set, and then re-applies only the file keys the environment did not touch. A variable therefore always wins, and the file still fills in everything else.

Writing a config file

Format is chosen by suffix: .toml, .yaml, .yml or .json. A missing file is an error, not a silent fall back to defaults.

# config.toml
[database]
path        = "~/.sqtseries/data/db.sqlite"
batch_size  = 2000

[ingestion]
port        = 12501
hwm         = 101000

[query]
port        = 12502
timeout_s   = 30.0
max_rows    = 10000

[http]
host        = "127.0.0.1"   # local-only; the default is 0.0.0.0
cors_origins = ["http://localhost:3000"]

[retention]
default_ttl = "90d"
# equivalent JSON
{
  "database": {"path": "~/.sqtseries/data/db.sqlite", "batch_size": 2000},
  "http":     {"host": "127.0.0.1"}
}

YAML needs pyyaml, which is not a declared dependency. TOML is built in and JSON goes through orjson; if you want YAML, install pyyaml or use TOML.

Environment variables

The prefix is SQT_SERIES_. Nest one level with a double underscore, so http.rate_limit_per_minute becomes:

$ export SQT_SERIES_HTTP__RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=42
$ export SQT_SERIES_DATABASE__BATCH_SIZE=500
$ export SQT_SERIES_CONFIG_FILE=/etc/sqtseries/config.toml

Names are case-insensitive, and an empty value counts as unset. So SQT_SERIES_DATABASE__PATH= with nothing after the equals means "use the default", not "use an empty path".

Ports, and why ingest is not the one you set

Six ports, five fixed and one chosen at start-up. This surprises almost everyone, so it is worth reading before you point a client at a number.

PortSocketBindsCarries
12500+auto-detected127.0.0.1 Ingest. The first free port in port_range_start…port_range_end, not the configured ingestion.port. Read the real one from sqtseries status or runtime.json.
12502ROUTER127.0.0.1 Query. One request frame in, one reply frame out. Wire-compatible with a plain REQ client.
12503XPUB127.0.0.1 Stream. Two-part frames, [topic, json]. XPUB, not PUB, so subscribe and unsubscribe events arrive on the wire and subscriber counts are exact.
12504REP127.0.0.1 Admin. {"cmd": …} in, a status envelope out.
12505HTTP + WebSockethttp.host HTTP. The REST API, the three WebSocket streams, the admin dashboard, these docs, and the self-hosted Swagger/ReDoc. Binds 0.0.0.0 by default, so a LAN machine can reach it.
12506PUB127.0.0.1 Stats. Connect, disconnect and subscription events, plus a periodic report. Two-part frames like the stream socket.
The ingest port is not the one you configured

With ports.auto_detect = true (the default) the ingest port is the first free port in the range, which is normally 12500 — not ingestion.port, which is 12501. A client hard-coded to 12501 works only when auto_detect = false or when 12500 is already taken. Always read the real ports from sqtseries status, or pass them from the same source your launcher used. The five fixed ports are reserved before the detector runs, so it can never hand out one of them.

The detector probes each candidate by binding 127.0.0.1 on it, then closing the socket and moving on. It is race-tolerant: if something takes the port in the gap between the probe and the real bind, the bind fails and you get a clean error rather than silent misdirection. The five fixed ports are reserved in the allocator before the detector runs, so it can never hand out one of them.

Running beside something else

Use port_offset to shift the whole detection window, or set auto_detect = false and pin ingestion.port yourself:

# a second instance: detection window 12600-12800
[ports]
auto_detect = true
port_offset = 100

# or pin everything, and fail loudly if it is taken
[ports]
auto_detect = false

[ingestion]
port = 12601

Duration values — two syntaxes

This is the single most common configuration mistake, and it is a mistake because there are two similar parsers with different rules.

Interval stringsTTL strings
Used by rollup.interval, backup.interval, maintenance.analyze_interval retention.default_ttl, retention.check_interval
Units accepted s m h d s m h d w
1m meansone minuteone minute
1w rejectedone week
Granularity of the effect how often the task runs retention drops whole monthly partitions, so a TTL is applied at month granularity whatever it says
There is no month syntax anywhere

Both parsers treat m as minutes. If you want "keep a year of data", write 365d or 52w — not 12m, which keeps twelve minutes and then drops whole monthly partitions, deleting far more than you intended.

[retention]
default_ttl     = "365d"   # a year — this is what you want
default_ttl     = "12m"    # twelve MINUTES — almost certainly a mistake

The database settings

These map onto SQLite's own file-level and per-connection settings. The defaults are what the shipped code uses; the notes explain the ones that look unusual.

KeyEnvironment variableDefaultWhat it does
database.pathSQT_SERIES_DATABASE__PATH ~/.sqtseries/data/db.sqlite The one SQLite file that holds everything. Parent directories are created. ~ is expanded.
database.page_sizeSQT_SERIES_DATABASE__PAGE_SIZE 8192 SQLite page size in bytes. Applied only when the file is created — SQLite cannot change it afterwards. It must be set before WAL, so the bootstrap connection skips WAL.
database.cache_sizeSQT_SERIES_DATABASE__CACHE_SIZE -64000 Page cache per connection, in KiB when negative. 8 MB on the shipped code path — see the note below on why this default is smaller than it looks.
database.mmap_sizeSQT_SERIES_DATABASE__MMAP_SIZE 268435456 Bytes of the file mapped into the address space (256 MiB). Reading through the mapping skips a copy from the page cache.
database.busy_timeoutSQT_SERIES_DATABASE__BUSY_TIMEOUT 5000 Milliseconds SQLite waits on a locked database before returning SQLITE_BUSY.
database.journal_size_limitSQT_SERIES_DATABASE__JOURNAL_SIZE_LIMIT 67108864 Bytes the WAL may keep after a checkpoint (64 MiB).
database.threadsSQT_SERIES_DATABASE__THREADS 4 SQLite worker threads.
database.batch_sizeSQT_SERIES_DATABASE__BATCH_SIZE 2000 Points per insert transaction. Must be 1…8191: above 8191 the batch can exceed SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER and a valid batch starts failing. A burst commits in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so a batch is all-or-nothing.
database.flush_intervalSQT_SERIES_DATABASE__FLUSH_INTERVAL 1.0 Seconds.
Why the page cache default is 8 MB, not 64 MB

The setting says -64000 (64 MB in KiB-negative form), but the code path applies cache_size = -8000 per connection instead, and that is deliberate. A 64 MB cache on a handle shared across executor threads makes glibc arena allocations balloon: pages cached on thread A's arena stay in A even when thread B later runs the same handle, because free() returns memory to its allocating thread's arena. Total resident memory then climbs roughly with threads times working set. Measured on 2026-09-09 at 10k pts/s: 60–100 MB anonymous arena mappings per handle in smaps, and anonymous memory growing about 25 MB per snapshot.

8 MB keeps the hot working set of a steady-state run resident per handle without the cross-thread duplication, and a miss falls through to the OS page cache, which is shared. A transient connection — one opened because every pooled reader is checked out — gets the same 8 MB rather than the full figure.

batch_size has a hard ceiling of 8191

A batch becomes one INSERT with a bound parameter per column per row, so it can run into SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER. Above 8191 the service refuses to start and says so, rather than failing every burst at 3 a.m.

Ports, ingest, query and HTTP settings

Every setting that decides where traffic goes, how much of it is accepted, and what happens when a client asks for too much.

KeyEnvironment variableDefaultWhat it does
ingestion.portSQT_SERIES_INGESTION__PORT 12501 Configured ingest port. Used as-is only when ports.auto_detect = false.
ingestion.hwmSQT_SERIES_INGESTION__HWM 101000 Receive high-water mark on the PULL socket. Frames buffer up to this before senders block, so a producer burst is absorbed rather than refused. Must be ≥ 1.
ingestion.pending_maxSQT_SERIES_INGESTION__PENDING_MAX 100 Batches outstanding between the receive loop and the persister. This is the backpressure point: at 100, the receiver stops reading and the socket's HWM takes over. Must be ≥ 1.
ingestion.max_message_sizeSQT_SERIES_INGESTION__MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE 52428800 Largest accepted frame in bytes (50 MiB). A larger frame is refused by the socket, not parsed.
ingestion.reject_client_timestamp_skew_sSQT_SERIES_INGESTION__REJECT_CLIENT_TIMESTAMP_SKEW_S 300.0 Seconds a client timestamp may differ from the server clock before the write is refused (400 over HTTP, counted invalid over ZMQ). Set 0 to accept any timestamp. This also sets how long an hour must be finished before the rollup will touch it, so a write can never land in an hour already summarised.
query.portSQT_SERIES_QUERY__PORT 12502 Query socket port.
query.timeout_sSQT_SERIES_QUERY__TIMEOUT_S 30.0 Seconds one query may run. Over HTTP the client gets 504; over ZMQ it gets QUERY_TIMEOUT. Also bounds one HTTP read. None or ≤ 0 disables the cap — the query still runs off the event loop.
query.max_rowsSQT_SERIES_QUERY__MAX_ROWS 10000 Hard cap on raw rows one query may materialise. Exceeding it is an error, never a silent truncation: 413 over HTTP, MAX_ROWS_EXCEEDED over ZMQ. 0 means unbounded. The check is a cheap COUNT(*) before the fetch, so an over-cap query never pays for the rows.
query.max_inflightSQT_SERIES_QUERY__MAX_INFLIGHT 64 Concurrent query dispatches. Past it, requests stay in the socket pipe (HWM-bounded) and are counted in queries_shed rather than spawning another handler. Must be ≥ 1.
streaming.portSQT_SERIES_STREAMING__PORT 12503 XPUB stream socket port.
streaming.linger_secondsSQT_SERIES_STREAMING__LINGER_SECONDS 30.0 Seconds a just-unsubscribed topic is remembered as "lingering" before it stops being reported. Keeps a flapping subscriber from flickering in the topic list.
streaming.topic_totals_maxSQT_SERIES_STREAMING__TOPIC_TOTALS_MAX 10000 How many recent topics keep a running publish total in memory. The counter is updated on the ingest path, so a producer using a new metric name per point would otherwise grow it without limit. The oldest topic is dropped past this cap; it still appears in the Topics panel (which unions this counter with the stored metrics) with its total shown as unknown. Must be ≥ 1.
admin.portSQT_SERIES_ADMIN__PORT 12504 Admin socket port.
stats.enabledSQT_SERIES_STATS__ENABLED true Run the stats publisher. Off means port 12506 is never bound.
stats.portSQT_SERIES_STATS__PORT 12506 Stats PUB socket port.
http.portSQT_SERIES_HTTP__PORT 12505 HTTP and WebSocket port.
http.hostSQT_SERIES_HTTP__HOST 0.0.0.0 Interface the HTTP gateway binds. The default is every interface, so a phone on the same network can open the dashboard. Set 127.0.0.1 for local-only. The five ZMQ ports stay loopback-only whatever this is set to.
http.cors_originsSQT_SERIES_HTTP__CORS_ORIGINS ["*"] Allowed browser origins. A list in TOML. There is no authentication, so * plus a non-loopback http.host means anyone who can reach the port can read and write. Narrow both on an untrusted network.
http.rate_limit_per_minuteSQT_SERIES_HTTP__RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE 600 Requests per minute per peer address, on a fixed one-minute window. Over the limit is 429. Must be ≥ 1. Keyed on the socket peer address; X-Forwarded-For is deliberately not trusted.
http.max_websocket_connectionsSQT_SERIES_HTTP__MAX_WEBSOCKET_CONNECTIONS 1000 Total live WebSocket budget across all three endpoints. A new connection past the cap is closed with code 1013. Must be ≥ 1.
ports.port_range_startSQT_SERIES_PORTS__PORT_RANGE_START 12500 First port the ingest detector may use.
ports.port_range_endSQT_SERIES_PORTS__PORT_RANGE_END 12700 Last port the ingest detector may use.
ports.auto_detectSQT_SERIES_PORTS__AUTO_DETECT true Pick the first free ingest port in the range. False means bind ingestion.port exactly and fail if it is taken.
ports.port_offsetSQT_SERIES_PORTS__PORT_OFFSET 0 Shift the whole detection range, so a second instance can run beside the first: 12500 becomes port_range_start + port_offset.

Background tasks and logging

The rollup, retention, maintenance and backup tasks, and how the service logs. Each task runs on boot and then on its interval, in a worker thread so a long pass never stalls the event loop.

KeyEnvironment variableDefaultWhat it does
rollup.enabledSQT_SERIES_ROLLUP__ENABLED true Keep the hourly summary table current. Off means wide queries scan raw rows, which is correct but slower.
rollup.intervalSQT_SERIES_ROLLUP__INTERVAL 5m How often the rollup task runs. An interval string (Ns/Nm/Nh/Nd), not a count of hours — 5m means "every five minutes", not "every five hours".
retention.enabledSQT_SERIES_RETENTION__ENABLED true Drop expired partitions automatically.
retention.default_ttlSQT_SERIES_RETENTION__DEFAULT_TTL 30d How long data is kept. A TTL string: s, m, h, d, w — so 4w is valid and 1m means one month, not one minute.
retention.check_intervalSQT_SERIES_RETENTION__CHECK_INTERVAL 1h How often retention runs. Also a TTL string.
retention.partition_intervalSQT_SERIES_RETENTION__PARTITION_INTERVAL month Partition width. Only month is supported. Retention drops whole partitions, so this is also the coarsest granularity at which anything is deleted.
maintenance.enabledSQT_SERIES_MAINTENANCE__ENABLED true Run periodic ANALYZE.
maintenance.analyze_intervalSQT_SERIES_MAINTENANCE__ANALYZE_INTERVAL 1h How often ANALYZE runs. An interval string.
backup.enabledSQT_SERIES_BACKUP__ENABLED true Snapshot on a schedule.
backup.intervalSQT_SERIES_BACKUP__INTERVAL 24h Seconds between snapshots. An interval string.
backup.pathSQT_SERIES_BACKUP__PATH ~/.sqtseries/backups/ Directory for snapshots. Created if absent. Each file is sqtseries-YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS.db; a name that already exists is kept, not overwritten.
logging.levelSQT_SERIES_LOGGING__LEVEL INFO One of DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL.
logging.formatSQT_SERIES_LOGGING__FORMAT console console for humans, json for a log collector.
logging.fileSQT_SERIES_LOGGING__FILE none Also write logs to this path. Unset means stderr only.
config_fileSQT_SERIES_CONFIG_FILE none Which settings file to load, when --config is not given. The only single-underscore variable: it is not a nested setting, so it has no __.
Turning a task off changes behaviour, not just timing

rollup.enabled = false is the one to think about. Queries stay correct — the rollup is an accelerator, not a source of truth — but a wide query then scans raw rows instead of summary rows, and that is a large, growing cost. The other three only change how often something tidies up.

What is refused at start-up

Every rule below is checked before the database is opened. A violation is an error naming the key, not a service that starts and then misbehaves.

RuleMessage shape
Every port in 1–65535 ingestion.port must be 1-65535, got 0
The six ports must all differ ports must be unique, got [12501, 12501, …]
ingestion.hwm ≥ 1 ingestion.hwm must be >= 1, got 0
ingestion.pending_max ≥ 1 ingestion.pending_max must be >= 1, got 0
query.max_rows ≥ 0 query.max_rows must be >= 0 (0 = unbounded)
query.max_inflight ≥ 1 query.max_inflight must be >= 1, got 0
database.batch_size in 1–8191 database.batch_size 9000 exceeds SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER safe limit of 8191
http.rate_limit_per_minute ≥ 1 http.rate_limit_per_minute must be >= 1, got 0
http.max_websocket_connections ≥ 1 http.max_websocket_connections must be >= 1, got 0
rollup.interval parses rollup.interval invalid: unsupported interval: 5x
maintenance.analyze_interval parses maintenance.analyze_interval invalid: …
retention.default_ttl and retention.check_interval parse retention invalid: invalid TTL: '30y' (use e.g. 30d, 12h, 4w)
backup.interval parses backup.interval invalid: …

Every violation is collected, not just the first, so one run tells you everything that is wrong.

The CLI flags

Two global flags apply to every command, and two subcommands take one flag of their own.

OptionArgumentDefaultWhat it does
--configPATHnone Settings file to load. .toml, .yaml, .yml or .json, chosen by suffix. A missing file is an error, not a silent fallback to defaults. The same value can come from SQT_SERIES_CONFIG_FILE.
--dbPATHnone Database file to use, overriding both the config file and SQT_SERIES_DATABASE__PATH. The value is the last override applied, so it wins over everything.
--versionnone off Print the version and exit.
--helpnone off Print the options for the group or the subcommand and exit.

Two of the subcommands take one flag of their own: install --system and uninstall --system install to /etc/systemd/system/ instead of the per-user ~/.config/systemd/user/.

CommandWhat it doesNeeds the service?
run Start the service in the foreground: opens the database, binds all six ports, starts the background tasks, prints where the dashboard, docs and health check live, then waits for SIGINT or SIGTERM. no — it is the service
stop Send SIGTERM to the pid in runtime.json, then wait up to 10 s for it to actually exit. Refuses to stop an instance whose database is not the one this invocation resolves. yes
status Print running/not-running, the pid, version, database path, the real bound ports, and the links. no
ports Print the active ports. With no service running, prints the configured ports and says so. no
health Run PRAGMA quick_check against the database. Prints ok and exits 0, or degraded: … and exits 1. no
stats Print the number of metrics and the number of series. Migrates the file first, so it works on a brand-new database. no
backup Write a consistent snapshot with VACUUM INTO into backup.path, named sqtseries-YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS.db. no — safe to run against a live service
optimize Run PRAGMA optimize to refresh query-planner statistics. no
vacuum Run a full VACUUM to shrink the file and rebuild the free pages. Cannot run inside a transaction, so stop the service first for anything large. recommended off
install Generate and install the systemd unit. no
uninstall Remove the systemd unit. no

Global options belong before the subcommand: sqtseries --config c.toml run, never sqtseries run --config c.toml.

Commands that touch the database all accept --db, so a one-off maintenance task against a different file needs no config file at all: sqtseries --db /path/to/other.sqlite health.

A complete config, every key once

Copy this as a starting point. Every key the loader reads is present, in file order, with its shipped default — so anything you change is a deliberate departure from what you just read.

# config.toml — every key, at its shipped default.
# Pass with: sqtseries --config config.toml run

[database]
path              = "~/.sqtseries/data/db.sqlite"
page_size         = 8192          # only applies when the file is created
cache_size        = -64000         # KiB; the code path uses 8000 per connection
mmap_size         = 268435456     # 256 MiB
busy_timeout      = 5000
journal_size_limit = 67108864     # 64 MiB
threads           = 4
batch_size        = 2000          # 1..8191; one transaction per batch
flush_interval    = 1.0

[ingestion]
port                        = 12501   # used only when auto_detect = false
hwm                         = 101000
pending_max                 = 100
max_message_size            = 52428800
reject_client_timestamp_skew_s = 300.0  # 0 disables the guard

[query]
port         = 12502
timeout_s    = 30.0          # 504 over HTTP, QUERY_TIMEOUT over ZMQ
max_rows     = 10000          # 0 = unbounded
max_inflight = 64

[streaming]
port            = 12503
linger_seconds  = 30.0

[admin]
port = 12504

[stats]
enabled = true
port    = 12506

[http]
host                      = "0.0.0.0"  # every interface; set 127.0.0.1 to be local-only
cors_origins              = ["*"]
rate_limit_per_minute     = 600
max_websocket_connections = 1000

[rollup]
enabled  = true
interval = "5m"            # interval string: s/m/h/d

[retention]
enabled           = true
default_ttl       = "30d"        # TTL string: s/m/h/d/w
check_interval    = "1h"         # TTL string
partition_interval = "month"      # only "month" is supported

[maintenance]
enabled          = true
analyze_interval = "1h"          # interval string

[backup]
enabled  = true
interval = "24h"           # interval string
path     = "~/.sqtseries/backups/"

[logging]
level  = "INFO"            # DEBUG|INFO|WARNING|ERROR|CRITICAL
format = "console"         # console|json
file   = ""                  # unset = stderr only

[ports]
port_range_start = 12500
port_range_end   = 12700
auto_detect      = true        # false = bind ingestion.port exactly
port_offset      = 0
Check it before you rely on it

Point the service at the file and ask. ports prints the values that will actually be used, which is the fastest way to catch a typo in a key name — an unrecognised key is ignored rather than reported, so a misspelling fails silently by design.

$ sqtseries --config config.toml ports

Security

Two facts decide how exposed the service is, and both are defaults rather than choices you made.

SurfaceBindsAuthentication
Five ZMQ ports127.0.0.1 only none — the loopback binding is the control
HTTP gatewayhttp.host, default 0.0.0.0 none — any request that reaches the port can read and write
WebSocketssame as HTTPnone

So on an untrusted network, both of these before you start:

[http]
host         = "127.0.0.1"
cors_origins = ["http://localhost:3000"]

That closes the service to the local machine. To serve other machines safely, leave it bound and put a reverse proxy in front that terminates TLS and authenticates. The response headers the gateway sets — X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, a strict Content-Security-Policy and a Permissions-Policy that denies camera, microphone, geolocation and payment — are all set on every HTTP response already.

The rate limiter keys on the socket peer address and deliberately does not trust X-Forwarded-For, because that header is set by the client and would let anyone rotate it to escape the limit. Behind a proxy, have the proxy do its own limiting.

Two different duration syntaxes

This is the single most common configuration mistake. Interval strings (rollup.interval, backup.interval, maintenance.analyze_interval) take Ns/Nm/Nh/Nd and nothing else. TTL strings (retention.default_ttl, retention.check_interval) take Ns/Nm/Nh/Nd/Nw and also accept w. In both, m means minutes — there is no month syntax anywhere. Retention additionally drops whole monthly partitions, so a TTL is applied at partition granularity.

Override order, lowest first

1. The default in the code. 2. The config file, from --config or SQT_SERIES_CONFIG_FILE. 3. Environment variables. 4. --db, which is applied last of all. The loader only lets the file supply a leaf the environment did not set, so a variable always beats a file.

Ports are resolved twice

The five fixed ports are read straight from settings. The ingest port may be reallocated by the detector. Always read the real values from sqtseries status rather than assuming.

Validation refuses to start

Every rule in validate_settings is checked before the database is opened. A bad value is an error message naming the key, not a service that starts and then misbehaves.

Security settings to review before exposing it

http.host defaults to 0.0.0.0 and http.cors_origins to ["*"], with no authentication on the HTTP side. On an untrusted network set both to loopback and put a proxy in front. The ZMQ ports are already loopback-only.

A full example, every section

The complete example further down this page sets every key once, with a comment on each, so you can copy a known-good starting point.

sqtseries — every setting, every file, every variable.

Every default on these pages is the default in the code, checked against sqtseries --help, the live settings loader and the running service by scripts/docs-build/verify_docs.py. The wire format is the same on every transport: ZMQ PULL, ROUTER, REQ, XPUB, HTTP and WebSocket.
